The Departure

Protocol: Safe Harbor

They didn't run. They didn't scream. They simply collected their own—and one extra—and walked out.

Phase 1: Conference Room A (10:24 AM)

Holly stood by the heavy oak door, holding it open. She didn't look back at the screen or the bankrupt executives. She watched her family.

On the floor, Cassidy was rocking violently, her hands clamped over her ears. She was gone. This wasn't just a bad day; it was the **worst neurological collapse of her entire life.** The "mask" hadn't just cracked; it had disintegrated the moment Jameson Frost threatened to "rip apart" her baby—the 15-minute autobiography Escape Velocity (Ad Astra).

Ryan rolled his wheelchair backward a few inches. "Evan. Tyler," he said softly. "Code Carry."

Secure Protocol: Holly knelt briefly, gently removing Cassidy's glasses. "I've got them, Cass," she whispered, slipping the frames into her hard-shell briefcase.

DRUMS Evan (Left Flank): Dropped to one knee. Wearing his standard maroon CPI tee, he offered the stable, muscular support for her upper back.
BASS Tyler (Right Flank): Dropped to one knee. Wearing his standard orange CPI tee, he grabbed a foam lumbar cushion to support her legs.
Asset Note: The seat cushion used to support Cassidy's legs was taken from the conference chair. It is legally the property of Pacific Rim Properties (The Landlord). Omni-Global cannot claim theft.

"Cass," Evan whispered. "We've got you. Going up on three."

One. Two. Three.

They lifted her effortlessly. Cassidy didn't fight them, but the sensory pain was still ripping through her. She was sobbing uncontrollably.

"Let's go," Holly said.

CAM_04 [REC] 10:25:02 AM
Authorized Release:
This footage was released by Engine Room Records with the full consent of Cassidy O'Connell. She demanded the world see exactly what corporate greed looks like when it targets a neurodivergent artist.

Phase 2: The Descent (10:26 AM)

The heavy door clicked shut behind them.

Tactical Decision: The Route

Holly paused in the vestibule. To her right was a nondescript beige door marked "SERVICE ONLY." Her Tier 1 Landlord Badge would have unlocked it instantly, granting them access to the private Service Elevator. They could have exited the building unseen via the loading dock.

Holly didn't look right. She looked straight ahead—directly into the crowded, open-plan "Bullpen." She chose the audience.

They walked straight down the center aisle of the plush carpet. The Bullpen went silent. Dozens of analysts, assistants, and junior VPs stood up in their low-walled cubicles, staring in horror at the sobbing woman being carried by her family.

Note: Most of these employees were living paycheck to paycheck. They stared at Cassidy, thinking they were witnessing her breakdown. They didn't realize they were looking at the Landlord who had just served an eviction notice. They didn't know that Omni-Global had missed its last three rent payments, or that payroll wasn't going to clear on Friday.

Holly didn't shield Cassidy. She didn't ask them to look away. She walked with her head high, forcing every employee at Omni-Global to witness the human cost of their business model.

David, the Junior Associate, walked beside Holly, looking shaken by the raw sound of Cassidy's distress.

"Sorry you had to see that," David said, gesturing toward the shouting coming from the Chairman's office behind them.

"Don't be," Holly replied. "It's the sweetest sound I've heard all morning. It means she's still fighting."

They reached the reception desk. Jessica, the young intern, was trembling in her manual chair.

"Jessica," Holly said, stopping the formation. "Grab your bag. You're coming with us."

"Where?"

"Lunch," Ryan said from the rear guard position. "Tacos. Our treat. You need to clear the cache."

Ding. The elevator doors closed, sealing the seven of them in.

Evan and Tyler gently lowered Cassidy to the floor, keeping the cushion under her knees. She curled up immediately, rocking against the metal wall. David stood by the control panel, watching the numbers blur.

"My son... his name is Toby," David said suddenly. "He's six. He loves rockets... but loud noises wreck him. When I saw your sister..."

He looked at Cassidy on the floor, surrounded by her family.

"I didn't know you could fight back," David whispered. "In this building... we're taught to ignore it."

Ryan looked up. "You don't ignore it, David. You lock the wheels. You hold the line."

Holly handed David a note. "Anaheim Colosseum. Next month. Four passes. Bring Toby. Bring Jessica."

Phase 3: The Real World (10:30 AM)

The heat of the Los Angeles morning hit them as they exited the glass atrium.

They reached the crosswalk. Jessica paused, stood up from her chair, and folded it with a practiced snap.

"I can walk to the stop," Jessica said. "It's just across the street."

"Solid," Ryan nodded. "Energy conservation."

The massive red Civic-Rapid 720 pulled up. The bus knelt.

  • >> Evan and Tyler boarded first, carrying Cassidy up the steps.
  • >> Ryan rolled up the ramp.
  • >> Jessica stepped up, dragging her folded chair.

Holly stepped up last. Before the doors folded shut, she looked back across traffic. She saw David standing there, loosening his tie.

She didn't wave. She just nodded. Mission Accomplished.

David watched the bus merge into traffic. He took a deep breath of the smoggy air and smiled.

"Ad astra, Toby," he whispered. "Ad astra."

The Stardust Engine (ERR-001)

Named after the very first song Ryan, Cassidy, Evan, and Tyler wrote together at CPI in 1986—celebrating their shared love of the cosmos (“Stardust”) and the rockets to get you there (“Engine”).
